title: above the clouds
description: Tres Piedras, New Mexico looks out to the east over the great expanse which is the Taos Gorge valley.

title: alpenglow at mineral creek with the adults after the babies have gone to sleep
description: A perfect day from a perfect trip. I sit down to paint just at twilight and sketch this out to bring home to Tres Piedras and finish painting while remembering the little ones bouncing around the tents and that rain storm an hour before and the crisp air and that cold, cold alpine river.

title: bottled lightning
description: On occasions, the electrons get out of balance. Randomly you just happen to be in that place at the wrong moment, right time and the atmospheres' electricity chooses to flow through your body.

title: does math control nature?
description: An exploration of the fibonacci sequence in nature, questioning whether mathematical patterns are the foundation of natural forms or merely our way of understanding them.

title: equilateral equilibrium
description: Rationing time and energy. The artifacts of ones life in need of attention and devotion. Finite existence demands decisions.

title: felt and lived
description: The convergence of experience and emotion, where opposing forces meet in the center to create something new and unified.

title: low angle sun rays
description: Wonder, about water vapor, dust and light angles. Effortlessly floating down the spine of the continental divide transporting moisture and spores. Aimlessly re-sculpting top soil creating art works while simultaneously eroding them like Buddhist monks and sand mandala's.

title: orbits (plankton dreaming of a sedimentary afterlife)
description: Recycling atoms. This year's compost growing next year's garden. Millennia of plankton floating in the ocean transforming nutrients and sunlight into sedimentary stone: actually forming earth.

title: out there, on the horizon, a solitary cloud
description: A proud cloud caught in the act of looking perfect while it though no one was looking. For three days straight I gazed at the clouds attempting to decoding their structures. The transparencies, translucency, opacity, luminosity and hues. The sky fades, how to think about that.

title: pollen and larvae
description: The dance of pollination and transformation, circles of life in geometric harmony.

title: separate, yet delicate, representations of existence
description: Living between chemical reactions and gravity. Believing in the balance of realities, that time is non-linear.

title: symbologies intertwine electronically
description: The modern intersection of ancient symbols and digital connectivity, where meaning flows through electronic pathways.

title: the algebra of water vapor
description: Clouds as mathematical equations, water vapor solving for x in the vast blue sky, where nature meets abstract calculation.

title: the atmosphere's electric finger
description: Behold the awe which is the blinding light of lighting strikes when surrounded by the intense darkness of encroached clouds while miles away from domesticated electricity.

title: the river in the sky
description: Magic is the transportation of millions of gallons of water over thousands of miles in the rivers of the atmosphere. Each molecule of water drifts aimlessly on a cyclical pilgrimage to the tops of the mounts only to erode their way back to the melting pot of the oceans.

title: towers
description: Looking up at clouds, seeing their magnificent height and perspective. The sky becomes architecture, water vapor transformed into towers reaching toward infinity.

title: triangular circles
description: Where geometry and emotion meet - perfect circle formed from sharp triangular fragments, suggesting wholeness through division.

title: twenty-one years
description: A celebration of time and growth, painted in arcs of vibrant color representing the journey through two decades of life and art.

title: two squared
description: An exploration of geometric form and balance, where two elements create a harmonious square composition.

title: Astro Bee
description: The intersection of space exploration and the natural world. An astronaut's helmet becomes a hive, bees navigating the cosmos within the human desire to explore beyond our atmosphere.

title: Autumnal Twilight
description: Concentric rings in thick impasto: the colors of the season going around — rose, ochre, slate, the last yellow — circling a warm center. The circle is the oldest mark we make, and I keep returning to it. This one is the light of an autumn evening, compressed into orbit. Oil on Panel, 2023.

title: Bottled Oxygen
description: Two bell jars share a hose: in one, a small yellow-leafed tree; in the other, a village of little dome houses, with a tap to meter the air between them. The tree works, the houses breathe. The future's utilities may be exactly this intimate.

title: Calavera Del Caballo
description: Jeannie holds a horse skull up to her face like a mask, like a question. The desert gives up its bones eventually, and they are beautiful — white architecture that once ran. Half a living face and half a dead animal's, sharing one gaze. Oil on Panel, 16 x 20 inches.

title: Combinations and Re-Entry
description: Third in the Geometric Anatomy series. The figure folds in on itself, hands over face, while the ground fractures into pastel triangles — the geometry pressing in closer this time.

title: Daydream
description: A small figure, chin in hand, with a cluster of crystal geometry blooming out of the head — and around it, nothing but open plate tone. That's the true anatomy of a daydream: mostly empty space, one bright formation.

title: Dayhike
description: A songbird with a backpack, ready for the trail (the plate is scratched 2018). The owl pioneered the look in 2016; word spreads fast in the forest.

title: Elephant Mask
description: Behind the bright yellow elephant mask: an elephant. "We all wear masks most of the time," the painting said back in 2018 — and the most convincing disguise is always yourself, slightly off.

title: First Contact
description: Now, I'm in the depths of contemplation about what lies ahead. A convergence of disparate events – my life to this point, the weight of age, the global tumult – swirl in my thoughts. Reflections on the past and musings on the future collide, sparked into focus by a bolt from the heavens.

title: Gardener
description: The whale tows a coracle planted with a tree — the print of Tugboat (Whale & Sequoia). The gardener of the future sea, mid-row, unhurried. Whales transplanting trees: I keep saying it because they keep doing it.

title: Geometric Anatomy
description: Two halves of my practice in a single frame: bodies painted as faithfully as I am able, intertwined against a field that has given up detail entirely — pale yellow broken by a red web of triangles.

title: Harmonics
description: A cloud, and the lightning under it, repeating like overtones of a single struck note. I was struck by lightning in September of 2023, and afterward I painted the sky differently — warily, respectfully, again and again.

title: In The Pines
description: Six pines, hand colored in six different greens, standing in their own quiet. Named for the place where shadows stack vertical and the needles make their own floor — and maybe a little for the old song.

title: Saber Tooth Puma
description: A puma carrying the old saber teeth again — the Pleistocene loadout reissued for the present mountains (the plate was first scratched in 2016). Deep time doesn't retire its designs; it just waits for the right climate to bring them back.

title: Shade Cloud
description: One small cloud far up, its patch of shade far below — and tucked into the shade, someone grateful. That's the entire economy of a desert summer: you learn to walk from one shadow to the next, and you thank the cloud personally.

title: The Meaning of Time
description: Inquiry into the conditions from which we enjoy the memory of our ancestors. Installation 2023. Included Works: Geometric Anatomy, Calavera Del Caballo, Cyclum Lunarem.

title: Tubed Pachyderm
description: An elephant refitted as a tube amplifier — vacuum tubes standing on its back, speaker cones set into its flank, a field of red gouache behind. The herd's volume restored by analog means. (I have opinions about analog; see the Olympus typewriter.)

title: Blue Corn
description: A tall figure stands very still on the orange ground, balancing an ear of blue corn on its head — and on the corn, an origami crane, also standing very still. Patience, practiced as agriculture. Corn is the oldest engineering project in this valley; see also the painting Three Blue Corn.

title: Continuation
medium: Acrylic, Latex and Oil on Canvas

title: Docile
description: Three monarchs lift a sledgehammer by kite strings.

title: Future Capacitor
description: Two heads meet at eye level. One is empty and pink; the other is packed with a branching network of nodes, charge waiting to move. A capacitor stores energy until the moment it is needed — so does a thought, so does a friendship. Sold at the April 2022 Art Hop in Truth or Consequences.

title: Ghost Thugs
description: There will always be individuals being individuals. Seven small ghosts in a lineup at the bottom of a scratched sky — and one of them, gold, clearly refusing the dress code.

title: Ken
description: At the beginning of our conversation that day, Ken told me Kathy had passed. We kept talking — a long, unhurried talk — and when it ended I took the photograph this painting comes from. I then spent tens of hours with his face, layering paint slowly, the way I do.

title: Nogal Canyon
description: I scratched this plate sitting in an arroyo in Nogal Canyon while on a camping trip with friends. This was near the windmill if you ever wanted to find the exact spot it would be down canyon from the windmill in the arroyo.

title: Olympus
description: This is one of my favorite typewriters of all time. Unfortunately it has a sticky "n" key, it works, but you get some type errors. That, though, is the cost of being analog!

title: Once Creatures Existed
description: Installation of Once Creatures Existed. Ruminations on the ever present world unfolding right before us. Twenty three paintings. October 2021 - January 2022. Desert Archaic, Truth or Consequences, New Mexico.

title: Origami Beetroot
description: A beet pulled and drawn like a botanical plate, its leaves creased flat and angular as folded paper. The garden produces its own origami; you just have to pull it up and turn it over. Intaglio Drypoint Print.

title: Rhino Radar (Arm Fauna)
description: A rhino patrols the outer perimeter looking for snacks while being aware of everything. Oil on Gesso Panel. Twelve by Sixteen Inches. Fall 2016, reworked 2022.

title: Rocket Propelled Clovis Point
description: A turtle carries the arsenal this time — rocket, clovis point, and satellite dish strapped to the hexagons of its shell. The slowest courier entrusted with the fastest cargo: twelve thousand years of point technology riding deep time's own armored chassis.

title: Saturday Evening Owls
medium: Acrylic, Latex & Paint marker on Canvas
description: I adore owls and hear them most places I sleep outside. I'm fascinated by the conversations they have late at night when the human world is asleep and night creatures are left to their explorations.

title: Skull
description: A skull in profile, hand colored a pale mineral green — the oldest still life subject there is. More curiosity than warning: this is the architecture under every portrait I've ever painted. Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

title: Space Owl
description: The owl, helmeted, antenna up. The owls already hold their conversations across the night (Saturday Evening Owls eavesdrops on them); this one has simply extended the broadcast range. Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

title: Submerged
description: A diver stands on the bottom, helmet line wandering all the way up to the thin band of the surface. Sibling of Deep Sea (2018) — the same predicament, revisited.

title: Sunflowers
description: Sunflowers in a mug, the big head spiraling with seed, hand colored in burnt orange. Numbered into the plate one pull at a time — an open-ended series, with each numbered print getting its portrait below. Intaglio Drypoint Print. Versions Each print is printed in an open ended series.

title: Surviving the Asteroid
medium: Oil, Oil Stick, Acrylic, Latex on Canvas
description: The crocodilians have seen an extinction or two and kept walking. Here one stands upright on the rust-red ground, grinning the grin of a survivor: not the fastest or the smartest, just impossible to finish off.

title: The Black Fire
description: A painting created in response to the Black Fire in the Aldo Leopold Wilderness during the spring of 2022. Oil on Linen. Twenty One by Thirty Four Inches. May 2022. In May of 2022 the Black Fire started near Diamond Creek in the Aldo Leopold Wilderness near Truth or Consequences, New Mexico.

title: Thread
description: Line work describes an angular hand on the right pulling a string emerging from the left vertical edge of the print.

title: Visible
medium: Acrylic, Latex and Oil on Canvas
description: A face caught in the instant of being seen — or of realizing it is seen. Painted fast and left raw, in a register my careful portrait work never allows: wide eyes, crimson and black, no time to compose yourself. Visibility is not always comfortable. Acrylic, Latex and Oil on Canvas. 30 by 24 inches.

title: airlift
description: Future cranes crafted from recycled libraries. They soar up on thermals. Voice heard echoing canyons. The float towards the sun. Find clouds along the way. Absconding back to the moon.

title: balance
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Printmaking on Rives BFK, Hand-colored with Gouache
description: Finding balance in the forest. Everything is something and is something else at the same time. All is connected and coincidence rules the day. Tomorrow I find myself ideal in balance and rhythm with the trees.

title: bison robotics
description: They will one day again roam the great plains. Three of them graze a pink-orange sky, hides of riveted sheet metal, legs of jointed steel.

title: butterfly conundrum
description: Based on the earlier oil painting: Butterfly Conundrum (2015).

title: cyclic repetition
description: The sacrifice of the drone bison. A future some days in front of us unfolding as echos we just now begin to hear. The bison have passed into the sunset. We missed them, so we brought them back as robots. They roamed again, autonomously. Year after year after year.

title: cydney and val
description: Cydney and Val in their masks from the DaDa Ball, one arm slung over a shoulder, two pairs of eyes looking out from behind turquoise paper-mâché. A portrait of mischief held still long enough to paint. Some faces you paint for the bones; these two I painted for the glint.

title: expansion drypoint
medium: Intaglio Drypoint Print on Rives BFK Paper
description: The mind shifts color pretending the future is a peeled orange imitating a banana. 8 x 10 inches paper Rives BFK

title: fall 2021
description: A log book of November 2021. Truth or Consequences, New Mexico The first days of November have brought perfect fall weather. The type of fall I always dreamed fall could be while a child in Montana. Lingering, wonderful fall. Work progresses on the new batch of paintings.

title: lunar lander
description: Based on an earlier 2014 oil painting of the same title (not yet documented here). Each print is printed in an open ended series. I physically scratch the print number into the plate before inking it and then print just one copy at that number.

title: molecule
description: Colorado Marble. 2019–Present. Some molecules just exist. Over in Europe the big atom smasher has allowed human knowledge to understand subatomic particles might be either matter or antimatter and effortlessly shift between those states.

title: owl
description: This painting was from a few years ago. I reworked this painting in April 2021 to how it is here. I have mixed feelings about working on old paintings.

title: paper neck giraffes
description: Paper neck giraffe. The rare breed of the future flatter than normal to use less water. These have the obligatory bonsai respirator apparatus which is oh so necessary in the futures climate.

title: Path Through the Autumn Leaves
description: Concentric squares in the colors of fall — orange, rust, a thread of turquoise sky — narrowing toward a small bright center. The sibling of Autumnal Twilight's circles: the same walk through the same season, this time with corners.

title: pink and yellow
medium: Oil, Oil Stick, Acrylic, Latex on Canvas
description: exploring the world between the worlds we float upon the land a horizon misting into the sky folding the trees into the earth

title: preservation cactus
description: A small cactus potted in a preservation jar, lid resting on top, not quite sealed. Painted thick, the whites like frosting. We put up the things we cannot bear to lose — peaches, memories, whole deserts if we could.

title: rocks glass
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-painted with Watercolor and Gouache
description: This particular glass was my grandfathers. He drank from it nightly a 7-up and vodka. 8 x 10 inches drypoint intaglio print hand painted with watercolor and gouache

title: stole the rainbow
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-painted with Watercolor and Gouache
description: Everyone is trying to find what is at the end of the rainbow. Some of us just have more effective tactics than others. 8 x 10 inches drypoint intaglio print hand painted with watercolor and gouache

title: the berry picker
description: Mika picking berries for the first time with her mother Selena. I fell in love with this image of Mika, her eyes staring straight into my being wide full of wonder and joy of that magic which is picking a huckleberry from the edge of a trail.

title: the mother bear
medium: Oil, Oil Stick, Acrylic and Latex on Canvas
description: Jeannie and I encountered this mother bear while hiking in to the Absaroka Mountains in Montana in August of 2021. We were headed up to Cowen Cirque to do a bit of alpine climbing for a few days and came upon this wonderful creature about 1 mile into the 10 mile hike.

title: there once was ice here
description: These polar bears, they learned how to blow glass and crafted mostly round bubbles to live in. They filled them with water and froze them solid and live inside one until it melts, escape and appear in the next bubble as if by magic. Or Imagination. Or space age teleportation technology.

title: transition
description: A nine-year painting. A tall, narrow column where big loose circles crowd the top and slowly resolve — band by band — into a small, orderly lattice of diamonds and dots at the bottom.

title: transplanter
description: Octopus tenderly tugging a coracle boat which has been planted with a magnificent Alligator Juniper tree.

title: tugboat whale sequoia
description: A sperm whale tows a coracle planted with a giant sequoia across a flat lavender sea. Whales transplanting trees — mutual aid at the scale the future will require. The tree is stressed but alive, and the whale knows where it's going.

title: vacation
description: A figure stands easy on green ground in a gold space helmet, oxygen tank resting at the knee. A vacation in the future may require equipment, but the posture is eternal: shoulders down, nowhere to be, air supply secured.

title: Alligator Juniper
description: The Nogal Canyon juniper, wind-bent and holding on. The third alligator juniper in the series — they are the great elders of this country, and I keep visiting them with a scribe point the way you visit grandparents with a camera. See also Nogal Canyon (2022). Intaglio drypoint prints.

title: Bonsai Giant Sequoia
description: The Sand hill Crane. Apocalyptic scavenger. They still wander the migrations paths of old and winter in the abundant Bosque del Apache along that ancient Rio Grande. Now they collect artifacts from defunct spaceships, the detritus of the Spaceport and human hubris.

title: Michael
description: Michael, mid-laugh, lit from one side against the dark — the kind of expression that lasts half a second and takes months to paint. I take the photograph first, then live with the face, layering until the person is present.

title: Migratory Scavengers
medium: Oil + 24kt gold leaf on ACM panel
description: Space program detritus and grain binge daydreams. Sandhill cranes on gold leaf — the old religious ground reserved for saints, here given to the scavengers who will inherit the launch sites. Companion piece to Bonsai Giant Sequoia, painted the same year.

title: Nana
description: Nana at the end of a century of weather, white hair lit like a cloud, one hand drawn up to her shoulder. The face is a map and I painted every road. Portraits of the very old are the closest my work comes to geology — time laid down in visible strata, and still moving. Oil on linen, 14x36 inches.

title: Rocket Propelled Clovis Point
description: A figure in a white suit stands at ease, helmet ringed with ears of corn, a single bee parked on the crown, holding a rocket-propelled clovis point.

title: Shawn Fischer
description: Of Flagship Romance Fame.

title: Solar Ascension
description: One large triangle built from a hundred small ones — reds, pinks, golds — rising off a green field like heat. The triangle is the sun's shape when a child draws its rays, and the oldest mark on the rock faces.

title: Solstice
description: Solstice (15 paintings). Algebraic assimilation. Harvests and desert flora. Substantial expansion. Mythological Intonations. Spacial Atoms. A group of 15 paintings.

title: Monsoon Bird
description: A bird built from the oldest vocabulary: striped body, wings of blue rain-leaves, a head of orange grid-marks around one concentric eye, arrows flying off the corner of the sky. It walks the red ground on stilt legs, the way the big birds do here when the water finally comes.

title: Prophets
medium: Site-specific Painting Installation on Found Wood
description: Site specific installation. Painting on Found Wood. Private collection.

title: Pruning
description: Loppers at work on a prickly pear, a green barrel cactus standing witness. Garden chores in the desert are a negotiation between species, and the cactus usually gets the last word. Hand colored. Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches, handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

title: Self Portrait
description: Wool cap, glasses, a gray gaiter against the cold — the artist at a precise moment in time, which is what I've said a self portrait is for. Mountain clothes, winter light, a face caught deciding something.

title: Six
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: Six round creatures on bird feet, eyes up on long stalks, hand colored in purples and blues, standing around the way a group does when nobody wants to leave first. Cousin to the Seven painting; apparently I count my crowds. Drypoint Intaglio Print, 8 x 10 inches. Handcolored with watercolor.

title: Tomorrow
description: Site Specific Installation, Las Cruces New Mexico.

title: Tomorrow
description: Site specific installation at Desert Archaic in Truth or Consequences, New Mexico.

title: 120 Volts
description: A long, stooped figure plugged into the wall outlet by his own hair. Household current as life support, five years before the sky demonstrated the high-voltage version on me personally. The glitch of daily reality at its most literal: we are all on the grid. intaglio printmaking on rives bfk.

title: A. Muscaria
description: Future perfect anomalies. The ants will probably be O.K. in that future perfect scenario. I'm guessing contingency plans are already in place. Winches. Now that was a giant leap forward for the ants.

title: Aeropress
description: The Aeropress, drawn like the small monument it is — exploded view, chambers stacked. Part of the coffee congregation, with the carafe and the espresso machine. 2018 plate 1 — the year started properly. intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018. private collection.

title: Airdrop
description: Future Cultures. Assimliated Gardens. Landscapes unquestionable.

title: Alligator Juniper
description: The juniper again, this time at arm's length: the trunk and limbs filling the frame, bark in checkered plates like reptile hide. You can know a tree from across the mesa or from inside its shade; this is the second kind of knowing. intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018.

title: Crystal Tooth Whale
description: Even mega fauna needs dental work.

title: Deep Sea
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: A figure in a diving helmet stands on the bottom, while a single line wanders all the way up to the thin green-and-red band of the surface, impossibly far above. Some days are like that. The air is up there somewhere. 8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

title: Elephant Mask
description: We all wear masks most of the time.

title: Field Theory AP
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-painted with Watercolor and Gouache
description: Concentric rectangles closing in on a small blue center — the field drawn as pure attention. The same image became a mural in Truth or Consequences; this is the pocket version. Artist proof. 8 x 10 inches. drypoint intaglio print. hand painted with watercolor and gauche. 2018.

title: Flicker Rhino
description: Airdrops in the night. This Rhino has it figured out. Friends with the Flicker feathers are affixed to a spider silk string. And upon the wind waves floats this Rhino of my dreams. Acrylic on Found Object. 13 x 20 inches. 2018. Private Collection.

title: Hands
description: Our hands allow us to be the most human we can. Acrylic on Found Wood. Dimensions Variable. 2018.

title: Kite
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: An elephant with her kite. Sometimes life is stranger than fiction. Pretending us humans with our myriad distractions would be the first to ever notice extra terrestrials is the kind of anthropocentric folly we are all to easily fooled by.

title: Lunarem
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: Twenty-eight moons in their phases, row by row, drawn from the years I spent painting the Earth's oldest timepiece (Cyclum Lunarem, 2014–2018). The moon repeats itself and is never the same twice — which is also a fair description of pulling prints from one plate. 8 x 10 inches.

title: Narwhal
description: Mystery of the sea. Where do you go? Where do you see? Acrylic on Found Object. 30 x 3.5 inches (approx). 2018. Private Collection.

title: Octobat
medium: Acrylic, Paint Marker and Latex Paint on Found Wood
description: Wild futures. An Octopus whom has created the most magical hot air balloon you could possible imagine. (I'm definitely pretty sure she sewed it by hand.) That Octopus, she is an acrobat so she is an octobat. An aquatic danced realized in the sky. Mesmerizingly absurd.

title: Pinned
description: Eight clouds, each one pinned to the sky with a nail, like specimens in a collector's drawer. In the desert you would do anything to make a cloud stay. So: pins. It works about as well as everything else we've tried. Acrylic and Latex on Canvas. 20 by 27 inches. 2018.

title: Prickly Pear
description: Prickly pear pads filling the square edge to edge, olive green on warm ochre, each one outlined like a river stone. A still life of the most ordinary desert citizen — the one that feeds you, sticks you, and outlives you.

title: Robot Family
medium: Oil, Oil Stick, Acrylic and Latex on Canvas
description: Two tall machines and a small one between them, holding hands, rolling on drawn wheels through a field of white and yellow. A family portrait from the far side of the future — whatever we become, apparently we still take the little one for a walk. One of the tender ones.

title: Seven
description: Seven white figures standing in a row, scraped and weathered into the gray like old fence posts, like cottonwoods in winter, like people waiting for something to begin. Count them and the title is done explaining; stand with them a while and it isn't. oil on canvas. 20 by 16 inches. Spring 2018.

title: Stole the Rainbow
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: Someone has cut the middle out of the rainbow and is walking off with it across the clouds, leaving the two ends standing there like an unfinished bridge. Hand colored, naturally — it's the only print where the color is the loot. Pulled again in 2021. 5 x 5 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print.

title: Teardrop
medium: Drypoint Intaglio Print, Hand-colored with Watercolor
description: The teardrop trailer — the Homemade Spaceship. Jeannie and I built one and lived in it for a year crossing the American West, so this is less a still life than a portrait of a home. Red and white, hand colored, permanently ready to leave. 8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print.

title: Tecate
description: A Tecate can, slightly crushed, hand colored red. The desert has its monuments and its sacraments; this one is both. Still life raises the authority of simple, mundane objects — sometimes the object is a cold beer at the end of a hot day. intaglio drypoint prints. printed area approx 6 x 9 inches.

title: Three Blue Corn
description: Three ears of blue corn, stacked like sleepers, every kernel its own small blue planet. Corn is the oldest technology in this valley — twelve thousand years of selective breeding before anyone called it engineering.

title: Thursday
description: A small hooded being with two dot eyes, alone in five by seven inches of fog. Painted on a Thursday, presumably; named for the most anonymous day of the week, the one nobody writes songs about. Some paintings are cathedrals. This one is a Thursday, and proud of it. oil on linen. 5 by 7 inches.

title: Cyclum Lunarem
medium: Oil and 24kt Gold Leaf on Gessoed Linen Panels
description: I painted the moons from an entire summer, starting on the summer solstice and completed on the autumnal equinox. Each moon is painted upon a 3 3/8" square prepared with linen and a traditional gesso ground. 24kt gold leaf was gilded upon this ground and the moon then painted upon this.

title: Riot Ghost
description: A ghost in a gas mask and wreath, standing in a scratched-black night. Even the dead come prepared now. From the Ephemera series' darker shelf — the glitches in daily reality include the evening news. intaglio drypoint prints. printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

title: Yellow and Orange
description: An orange triangle on a yellow field. Oil on Gesso Panel. Twelve by Fourteen Inches. Winter 2017.

title: Air Lift
description: Two hot air balloons cooperate to lift one untroubled elephant. The first appearance of an airlift I kept returning to — the plate was pulled again in 2021. Some problems simply require more balloons. 5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

title: Alligator Juniper (Adobe Canyon)
description: A whole alligator juniper, drawn limb by limb, the checkered bark that names the species rendered scratch by scratch. The drypoint scribe turns out to be the right tool for a tree that grows one century at a time. 8 x 10 inches. Intaglio Drypoint Print. Spring 2016. private collection.

title: Approximate Completion
description: Rings of purple, magenta, and red circling a pale center, like a storm seen from above or a tree's rings still being laid down. The title is the whole philosophy of my abstract work: each pass approximates closer that perfection in form which I will never attain but will always strive towards.

title: Boom Box
description: A skull-faced figure in a space helmet carries a boombox on one shoulder, walking the horizon line. Every era gets the procession it deserves; ours brings its own soundtrack and its own helmet. 5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

title: Day Hike
description: An owl wearing a backpack, ready for the trail. The work of a day hike is mostly looking — and nobody looks like an owl. A backpacked songbird took up the same hobby in Dayhike (2023). 5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

title: Spring
medium: Oil and Spray Paint on Linen
description: Triangles in every green the season makes — plus one or two orange ones for the early bloomers — scattered across a gray field like seedlings coming up through late snow. Spring arrives geometrically if you watch closely: one point first, then the spread. Oil and Spray Paint on Linen.

title: Binoculars
description: A creature that is mostly neck — a long striped column rising out of ordinary baggy trousers — with binoculars for a head. All watcher, no talker. I have spent enough of my life glassing ridgelines that this may be a self portrait of one particular muscle. 20 by 30 inches. Oil on Panel.

title: Cadence
description: Forty-nine orange circles in a careful grid, each one drawn around and around like a tiny enso. Cadence is what repetition becomes when you stop counting — the hand finds the rhythm and the rhythm keeps the hand. The same mark, made until it sings. 13 by 13 inches. Oil on Gesso Panel. Walnut Frame.

title: Clouds
description: A terracotta profile face, eyes closed, gathering a crowd of small white spheres — clouds in the shape thoughts take when you finally lie down in the grass and look up. They cluster at the lips and crown like a hatch of weather. Where clouds come from, more or less. 8 by 13 inches. Oil on Linen.

title: Egg
description: A figure folded into itself inside a red oval — knees up, arms wrapped, the body becoming the shapes it's made of. Everything waiting to begin is egg-shaped, including us.

title: Enso
description: Three ensos — the circle drawn in one continuous gesture, here built up in yellows, greens, and pinks like tree rings. I lived three years in a monastery and the enso followed me home: the mark that records exactly one moment of one hand, never repeatable, never finished.

title: Rainfall
description: Monsoon hovering; bored on the horizon. Prelude: It's been some years now that I've been in the desert and it's motions have solidified in my veins pulsing with blinding white intensity.

title: Split the Atom
description: A head split and split again, fanned out like a deck of cards: skin, then muscle, then skull, and at the very center a blue coil of whatever-it-is that does the looking. Split the atom and you get energy; split the self and you get this — layer after layer, each one wearing the one beneath.

title: Substantial
description: A wall of gray faces, all enormous eyes, watching a small figure who has turned to leave the frame. Being seen is heavy — substantial — and so is deciding to walk out from under it. Years later Visible picked the same nerve from the other side. 13 by 21 inches. Oil on Linen. 2015.

title: Arm Fauna
description: I painted this on the occasion of reading about the death of Satao. I had not known before of this creature but his story really moved my heart. So I gave this elephant a rocket so as he might ever so slightly even the playing field.

title: Atmospheric Whales
description: Whales coming down by parachute through a gold-leaf sky, an eye-sun watching from above. They appear again and again in my work, these atmospheric whales — the biggest body the planet ever made, handed the gentlest possible landing. Five by seven inches of the largest thing I know. 5 by 7 inches.

title: Bison at Sunset
description: A golden, glowing rider on a dark bison, crossing the last light at the bottom of a night-blue sky. The oldest partnership on the plains, painted small and quiet. Some paintings want to be murals; this one wanted to be a secret. 8 by 13 inches. Oil on Linen. 2014. Private Collection.

title: Coffee Carafe
description: A white enamel carafe, dented by use, doing what it has done every morning for decades. Still life paintings raise the authority of the simple, mundane objects whose presence infuses our being — and few objects have infused mine more reliably than the coffee vessels.

title: Corn Sky Connection
description: The spark from the heavens sets the maize to life.

title: espresso machine
description: The espresso machine painted white on white, an appliance dissolving into the kitchen light like a saint in an old fresco. Every household has its altars. This is one of ours. 8 by 8 inches. Oil on Panel. 2014. Private Collection.

title: Expansion
description: The mind shifts color pretending the future is a pealed orange imitating a banana. Six by Seven Inches. Oil on Handwoven Linen. Summer 2014.

title: Pet Walk
description: A figure in a space helmet takes a small whale for a walk on a leash, across a gold field under a deep teal sky. In some future, this is just Tuesday. The tenderness is the point: whatever world we end up in, somebody will still walk the pet. 5 by 7 inches. Oil on Handwoven Linen. 2014.

title: Dodecahedron
description: The inspiration for this Buddha comes from a small wooden carving of the Buddha in the Temple of Namgyal Monastery, Dharamshala India.

title: Parasitic Pollen Eaters
description: The bees build bubbles to protect themselves from the poisons dropped by drones on the human's crops. The bubbles allow them to gather pollen while not being infected.

title: Me Own Juniper
description: Alive prominently upon a height of land out on one of a myriad of mesas extending west from the crest of the Black Range in Southern New Mexico there exists this particular Alligator Juniper. Splendid and ancient, all full of stories reaching as far back as any living being in these parts remembers.

title: Muxy
description: Painted while working at Showdown Ski Area in the heart of the Little Belts up in cold wonderful Montana. This is the place of my youth and it was a magical summer Jeannie and I spent up there.
